I wished that Hitler would come and with his fiery people, tear open the heart of this wretched earth, in which the existence of impure humans would be incinerated. It was as if the whole world had set out to provoke me. Any sapling I plant, is it possible that the merciless claws of chickens would not scratch it? Any flower I pick, why wouldn't it appeal to my dead friends, and why wouldn't they make it the adornment of their hair buns? In short, the world has become hostile to my every word and deed. And how small is my world! Just these few lost souls, two or four second-hand lovers, and some crude, quarrelsome, and fashion-obsessed friends. Is this even a world? भस्म.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit भस्मन् (bhasman), specifically from the nominative singular भस्म (bhasma).

senses.gloss: sound of distress, affliction, or fear

हा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀳𑀸 (hā), from Sanskrit हा (hā), ultimately of onomatopoeic origin.

senses.gloss: to make an end of, consume, exhaust
to make, achieve, accomplish, complete, perfect

सारना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit सारेइ (sārei, “to make move, remove”), from Sanskrit सा॒रय॑ति॒ (sāráyati), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *sāláyati, from Proto-Indo-European *sol–éye-ti, the causative of the root *sel- (“to spring, jump”). Related to सरकाना (sarkānā), सरसराना (sarsarānā), पसा…

सारा.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀸𑀭 (sāra, “all, whole”), from Sanskrit सार (sā́ra, “best part”).

सारा.etym: Borrowed from Arabic سَارَة (sāra), from Biblical Hebrew שָׂרָה (śārâ, “lady, princess”).

दुनिया.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دنیا (dunyā), from Arabic دُنْيَا (dunyā). Compare Bengali দুনিয়া (duniẏa), Dhivehi ދުނިޔެ (duniye), Gujarati દુનિયા (duniyā), Marathi दुनिया (duniyā), Punjabi ਦੁਨੀਆ (dunīā).

जैसा.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi जैसा (jaisā), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑀇𑀲 (jaïsa), from Sanskrit यादृश (yādṛśa). Cognate to Punjabi ਜਿਹਾ (jihā).
Inherited from Old Hindi जैसा (jaisā), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑀇𑀲 (jaïsa), from Sanskrit यादृश (yādṛśa). Cognate to Punjabi ਜਿਹਾ (jihā).

ही.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit हि (hi, emphatic particle) likely with some other particle such as एव (eva, “indeed”) or वै (vai, “indeed”). Compare the functionally equivalent Gujarati જ (ja), Marathi -च (-ċ) (whence Bombay Hindi -ईच (-īc)).

छेड़ना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *छेडइ (cheḍaï) or *चेडइ (ceḍaï), the causative of *चिडइ (ciḍaï) / *चिढइ (ciḍhaï, “is angry”), which is the source of Hindi चिड़ना (ciṛnā) / चिढ़ना (ciṛhnā, “to be annoyed”). Of ultimately uncertain origin.

लगाना.etym: Causative form of लगना (lagnā) with the suffix -आना (-ānā).

पंजा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پنجه (panja). Doublet of पाँच (pā̃c, “five”).

कुरेदना.etym: With the variants कुरेलना (kurelnā), कुरोदना (kurodnā), from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *कुर- (kura-, “scraping”) with some suffix extensions. Cognate with Punjabi ਕੁਰੇਲਣਾ (kurelṇā, “to poke”), Marathi कुरचणे (kuracṇe, “to nip off with the nails”). Probably related to खुरचना (khurac…

छोड़ना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀙𑁄𑀟𑁂𑀤𑀺 (choḍedi). Cognate with Sindhi ڇوڙڻُ (choṛṇu) / छोड़णु, Gujarati છોડવું (choḍvũ), Marathi सोडणे (soḍṇe).

फूल.etym: Cognates include Assamese ফুল (phul), Bengali ফুল (phul), Bhojpuri फूल (phūl), Gujarati ફૂલ (phūl), Maithili फूल (phūl), Marathi फूल (phūl), Nepali फूल (phūl), Odia ଫୁଲ (phula), Punjabi پھل / ਫੁੱਲ (phulla), and Sindhi ڦل (phulu).

फूलना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀨𑀼𑀮𑁆𑀮𑀤𑀺 (phulladi), from Sanskrit फुल्लति (phullati). See फूल (phūl, “flower”) for more. Cognate with Assamese ফুলা (phula).

चुनना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit चुणइ (cuṇaï, “pecks up”), a variant of चिणेइ (ciṇei, “to gather, collect”) perhaps from contamination with गुहइ (guhaï, “strings together”). Ultimately from Sanskrit चिनोति (cinoti, “arranges”). Doublet of चिनना (cinnā). Cognate with Gujarati ચુણવું (cuṇ…

भला.etym: Inherited from Prakrit भल्लय (bhallaya), from Sanskrit भल्ल (bhalla, “auspicious, favourable”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-).
Inherited from Prakrit भल्लय (bhallaya), from Sanskrit भल्ल (bhalla, “auspicious, favourable”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-).

क्यों.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi क्यूं (kyūṃ), from Apabhramsa किंव (kiṃva), केंव (keṃva), from the interrogative base in क्- (k-) + एंव (eṃva), for which see यों (yõ).

वो.etym: Most likely from Old Hindi उहु (uhu), उहुं (uhuṃ), from Apabhramsa ओहु (ohu), from Prakrit 𑀅𑀳𑁄 (aho), from Sanskrit असौ (asáu, “that”). The inflected forms are formed by analogy with its proximal counterpart यह (ya).

मरना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀫𑀭𑀇 (maraï), from Sanskrit मर॑ति (márati). Cognate with Nepali मर्नु (marnu).

भाना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀪𑀸𑀤𑀺 (bhādi), from Sanskrit भाति (bhā́ti, “to shine, gleam”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰáHti, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰéh₂-ti. Cognate to Marathi भावणे (bhāvṇe), Gujarati ભાવવું (bhāvvũ).

जूड़ा.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑀽𑀟 (jūḍa), from Sanskrit जूट (jūṭa, “roll of hair”).

बनाना.etym: Regular causative form of बनना (bannā). Compare Marathi बनवणे (banavṇe).

हर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian هر (har). Doublet of सब (sab) and सर्व (sarv). Compare Bengali হর (hor), Punjabi ਹਰ (har).

बैर.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit वैर (vaira, “enmity”), vriddhi-form of वीर (vīrá, “hero”).

कितना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit *कियत्त (*kiyatta), variant of Sanskrit कियत् (kíyat), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kíHant, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷíh₂-onts, from *kʷíh₂, neuter of *kʷís. Cognate with Ashkun ćīt, Waigali kiti, Avestan 𐬗𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬧𐬙 (cuuaṇt), Latin quantum.

आशिक़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian عَاشِق (āšiq), from Arabic عَاشِق (ʕāšiq). Compare Bengali আশেক (aśeq) / Bengali আশিক (aśiq).

मिज़ाज.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مزاج (mizāj), from Arabic مِزَاج (mizāj, “temperament”).

बिलकुल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بِالْکُلّ (bi-l-kull), Arabic بِالْكُلّ (bi-l-kull).

थकना.etym: Inherited from Apabhramsa थक्कइ (thakkaï), from Prakrit 𑀣𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀇 (thakkaï), denominal verb from 𑀣𑀓𑁆𑀓 (thakka), from Sanskrit स्थ (stha), from स्था (sthā), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-.

नीचा.etym: Derived from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀡𑀺𑀘𑁆𑀘 (ṇicca) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit नीच (nīcá), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *niHćás (“facing down”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *niHčás, from Proto-Indo-European *ni-h₃kʷ-ós, from *ní (“down”) + *-h₃kʷ- (“facing, looking”).

दूर.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀽𑀭 (dūra), from Sanskrit दूर (dūrá). Also influenced by Classical Persian دور (dūr).
Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀽𑀭 (dūra), from Sanskrit दूर (dūrá). Also influenced by Classical Persian دور (dūr).

अब.etym: Inherited from Prakrit एव्वं (ĕvvaṃ), from Sanskrit एवम् (evam), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háywa-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óy-w-o-. Cognate with Bengali এবে (ebe).

धूल.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit धूलि (dhūli), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *dʰuHliṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰuHliš, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂lis, from *dʰewh₂- (“smoke”). Cognate with Lithuanian dúlis (“mist”) and Latin fūlīgō. Doublet of धूलि (dhūli), a tatsama.

उड़ना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi उडना (uḍanā), from Prakrit 𑀉𑀟𑁆𑀟𑁂𑀇 (uḍḍei), from Sanskrit उड्डयते (uḍḍayate). Cognate with Punjabi ਉਡਣਾ (uḍaṇā), Nepali उड्नु (uḍnu), Gujarati ઊડવું (ūḍavũ), Marathi उडणे (uḍṇe), Bengali উড়া (uṛa).

पैदा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پیدا (paidā). First attested as Old Hindi पैदा (paidā). Cognate with Bengali পয়দা (poẏoda).

ताल्लुक़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تعلق (ta'alluq), from Arabic تَعَلُّق (taʕalluq). Compare Punjabi ਤੱਲਕ (tallak) / تعَلُّق (tʻalluq). Related to मुतअल्लिक़ (mutaalliq).

कहना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi कहना (kahanā), from Prakrit कहेइ (kahei), कधेदि (kadhedi), from Sanskrit कथयति (kathayati). Cognate with Bengali কহা (koha), কওয়া (koōẇa) and Assamese কোৱা (küa), Sinhalese කියනවා (kiyanawā).

वक़्त.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian وَقْت (waqt), from Arabic وَقْت (waqt). Compare Bengali ওয়াক্ত (ōẇakto), Punjabi ਵਕਤ (vakat), Santali ᱚᱠᱛᱚ (ôktô).

फिरना.etym: Cognate with Punjabi ਫਿਰਨਾ / پِھرنا (phirnā), Gujarati ફરવું (pharvũ), Marathi फिरणे (phirṇe), Bengali ফেরা (phera).

क्या.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀓𑀺𑀁 (kiṃ), 𑀓𑀺 (ki), from Sanskrit किम् (kim, “what, which”). Compare Punjabi ਕੀ (kī), Gujarati કિયું (kiyũ), Marathi की (kī), Bengali কী (ki), Assamese কি (ki) or Kashmiri کیاہ.

चीज़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian چِیز (čīz, “object, thing, stuff”). Compare Punjabi ਚੀਜ਼ (cīz) / چِیز (cīz), Gujarati ચીજ (cīj), Marathi चीज (cīj), Nepali चिज (cij), Bengali চিজ (cij).

लेकिन.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian لیکِن (lēkin), from Arabic لٰكِنْ (lākin).

ज़माना.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زمانه (zamāna), from Middle Persian [script needed] (ẕmʾnk' /⁠zamānag⁠/). Compare Punjabi ਜ਼ਮਾਨਾ (zamānā) / زَمانہ (zamānh), Gujarati જમાનો (jamāno), Marathi जमाना (jamānā), Bengali জমানা (jomana).

जब.etym: From अब (ab, “now”). Cognate with Punjabi ਜਦੋਂ (jadõ) / جدوں (jadõ).

सुनना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit सुणइ (suṇaï), from Sanskrit शृणोति (śṛṇoti), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćr̥náwti, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱl̥néwti. Cognate with Nepali सुन्नु (sunnu) and Assamese শুনা (xuna), and distantly with Irish cluin (“to hear”).

दिया.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀻𑀯 (dīva), from Sanskrit दीप (dīpa). Cognate to Punjabi ਦੀਵਾ (dīvā), Nepali दियो (diyo), Gujarati દીવો (dīvo), Marathi दिवा (divā). Doublet of दीप (dīp) and दीपक (dīpak).

दिल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دِل (dil). First attested as Old Hindi दिल (dila). Doublet of हृदय (hŕday) and हिया (hiyā).

हमदर्दी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian ہَمْدَرْدی (ham-dardī). By surface analysis, हमदर्द (hamdard, “sympathy”) + -ई (-ī).

लहर.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀮𑀳𑀭𑀻 (laharī), from Sanskrit लहरी (laharī), लहरि (lahari).

मारना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit मारयति (mārayati), from the root मृ (mṛ). Cognate with Nepali मार्नु (mārnu), Assamese মাৰা (mara).

ख़ाब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خْوَاب (xwāb), from Middle Persian 𐭧𐭥𐭠𐭡 (ḥʿʾb). Doublet of सपना (sapnā) and स्वप्न (svapna), both ultimately being from Sanskrit स्वप्न (svapna). Cognate with, Bengali খোয়াব (khōẇab), Punjabi ਖ਼੍ਵਾਬ (xvāb) / ਖ਼ਵਾਬ (xavāb), Gujarati ખ્વાબ (khvāb).

मुल्क.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مُلْک (mulk), from Arabic مُلْك (mulk). First attested as Old Hindi मुलक (mulaka).

बेहतर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بِهْتَر (bihtar). False cognate of English better.

चुकना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀘𑀼𑀓𑁆𑀓𑀇 (cukkaï), denominal verb from 𑀘𑀼𑀓𑁆𑀓 (cukka), from Sanskrit च्यु॒त (cyutá), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čyutás, from Proto-Indo-European *kyu-tós, from *kyew- + *-tós. Doublet of चूकना (cūknā).

जज़्बात.etym: Borrowed from Arabic جَذْبَات (jaḏbāt), plural of جَذْب (jaḏb) (whence जज़्बा (jazbā)).

जज़्बा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جذبه (jazba, “allure, appeal, charm”), from Arabic جَذْب (jaḏb, “attraction, seduction”), from the verb جَذَبَ (jaḏaba, “to charm, to attract”).

मज़हब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مذهب (mazhab), from Arabic مَذْهَب (maḏhab).

ग़र्क़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian غَرْق (ġarq), from Arabic غَرْق (ḡarq).

घोड़ा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit घोडय (ghoḍaya), from Sanskrit घोटक (ghoṭaka), possibly from Proto-Dravidian *kut-ir-ay (“horse”), from *kuti (“to jump”), from *kut + *i.

टापना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit *त्रपति (*trapati) ~ *तर्पति (*tarpati), from the root त्रप् (trap, “to feel; to leap”). Cognate with Punjabi ਟੱਪਣਾ (ṭappaṇā) / ٹَپَّݨا (ṭappaṇā), Sindhi ٽرَپَڻُ (ṭrapaṇu) / ट्रपणु (ṭrapaṇu), Saraiki ترَپَّݨ (trappaṇ), Nepali टप्नु (ṭapnu), Gujarati ટપવ…

ज़्यादा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زِیَادَه (ziyāda), from Arabic زِيَادَة (ziyāda). Compare Bengali জেয়াদা (jeẏada), Gujarati જ્યાદા (jyādā), Marathi जादा (jādā), Punjabi ਜ਼ਿਆਦਾ (ziādā).

असर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اثر (asar), from Arabic أَثَر (ʔaṯar).

कुर्सी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian کُرْسِی (kursī), from Arabic كُرْسِيّ (kursiyy).

झूमना.etym: Unknown. Maybe from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *झुंभ- (jhuṃbha-), an unattested variant from खुंभ- (khuṃbha-, “to shake”), from Sanskrit क्षु॒भ्नाति॑ (kṣubhnā́ti), from क्षुभ् (kṣubh, “to shake”). The initial could be from influence by झपटना (jhapaṭnā), झट (jhaṭ).

कौन.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Apabhramsa कवन (kavana), from Sanskrit कपुन (kapuna, “who”). Compare Gujarati કોણ (koṇ), Marathi कोण (koṇ), Bengali কোন (kōn). See किस (kis) for more.

राहत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian رَاحَت (rāhat), borrowed from Arabic رَاحَة (rāḥa), from رَاحَ (rāḥa). First attested in c. 1586 as Middle Hindi راحت (raḥt /⁠rāhat⁠/).

अंदर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اندر (andar), from Middle Persian 𐭡𐭩𐭭 (andar). Doublet of अंतर (antar).

senses.gloss: a mine; a rich source; store, treasury; multitude

तख़्त.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تَخْت (taxt, “throne”), from Middle Persian tʾht' (taxt), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover”). Compare Punjabi ਤਖ਼ਤ (taxat).

बैठना.etym: Denominal verb from Prakrit उवविट्ठ (uvaviṭṭha) + -ना (-nā) with the aphaeresis of /u/, ultimately from Sanskrit उपविश् (upaviś, “to enter, sit”).

senses.gloss: ye, you (formal, polite and grammatically plural)

आप.etym: Cognate with Gujarati આપું (āpũ), Nepali आंत (ānta), Marathi आपण (āpaṇ), Bengali আপনি (apni), Sinhalese අපි (api). Compare Kamkata-viri amú (“self”), Dhivehi އަހަރެން (aharen̊). Distantly cognate with Old English ǣþm, Dutch adem (“breath”), and German Atem (“breath”). Doublet …

मोम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian موم (mōm, mūm). Compare Bengali মোম (mōm), Punjabi ਮੋਮ (mom).

देखना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit देक्खइ (dĕkkhaï), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀤𑁂𑀔𑀢𑀺 (dekhati /⁠dekkhati⁠/), from Sanskrit *द्रक्षति (*drakṣati), from दृश् (dṛś), possibly influenced by प्रेक्ष॑ते (prékṣate).

नन्हा.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi नन्हा (nanhā), नान्हा (nānhā), from Prakrit लण्ह (laṇha) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit श्लक्ष्ण (ślakṣṇá, “soft, smooth”). The assimilation of initial l- to n- is seen in a handful of other terms; compare नुचना (nucnā).

senses.gloss: darling, dear, boy (especially of a child)

मुन्ना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀫𑀼𑀁𑀟 (muṃḍa) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit मुण्ड (muṇḍa). Cognate with Punjabi ਮੁੰਡਾ (muṇḍā), ਮੁੰਨਾ (munnā).

खेल.etym: Deverbal form of खेलना (khelnā, “to play”). Cognate with Marathi खेळ (kheḷ).

खेलना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit खेलइ (khelaï, “to play”), 𑀔𑁂𑀮𑀡 n (khelaṇa, “playing”), of uncertain further origin. See there for more. Cognate with Nepali खेल्नु (khelnu), Marathi खेळणे (kheḷṇe), Konkani खेळ्चे (kheḷce), Bengali খেলা (khela), and Assamese খেলা (khela). Related to Roma…

कूदना.etym: Cognate with Punjabi ਕੁੱਦਣਾ (kuddaṇā), Gujarati કૂદવું (kūdvũ), Marathi कुदणे (kudṇe), and Bengali কুঁদা (kũda), and further related to Tamil குதி (kuti), Malayalam കുതിക്കുക (kutikkuka).

मक़सद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مَقْصَد (maqsad), from Arabic مَقْصَد (maqṣad). Compare Bengali মকসদ (mokśod).

senses.gloss: life (as in the state of being alive)

ज़िंदगी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زندگی (zindagī). Compare Bengali জিন্দেগি (jindegi), Punjabi ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ (zindgī), Tamil ஜிந்தகி (jintaki, “property”).

किताब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian کِتَاب (kitāb), borrowed from Arabic كِتَاب (kitāb). Displaced Old Hindi कतेब (kateba), from the same source.

अम्माँ.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀅𑀁𑀫𑀸 (aṃmā), 𑀅𑀁𑀩𑀸 (aṃbā), from Sanskrit अम्बा (ambā́). Doublet of अंबा (ambā), a tatsama.

पूरी.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀽𑀭 (pūra) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀇𑀓𑀸- (-ikā-), from Sanskrit पूर (pūra, “cake”). Compare Sanskrit पूरिका (pūrikā).

भाई.etym: Cognate with Punjabi ਭਰਾ (bharā) / بھرا (bharā), Sindhi भाऊ / ڀاءُ (bhāū), Gujarati ભાઈ (bhāī), Marathi भाऊ (bhāū), Bengali ভাই (bhai), Persian برادر (barâdar), Ancient Greek φράτηρ (phrátēr), Latin frāter, Old Norse bróðir and Old English brōþor (English brother).

तल्ख़ी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تلخی (talxī). By surface analysis, तल्ख़ (talx) + -ई (-ī).

कहा.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀓𑀳𑀸 (kahā), from Sanskrit कथा (kathā).

तुम.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Apabhramsa तुम्हि (tumhi), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀢𑀼𑀫𑁆𑀳𑁂 (tumhe), from Sanskrit युष्मान् (yuṣmān, “you”, acc. pl.) adopting the initial sounds of त्वम् (tvam, “you”, nom. sg.).

मतलब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مطلب (matlab), from Arabic مَطْلَب (maṭlab).

ज़मीर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian ضمیر (zamīr), from Arabic ضَمِير (ḍamīr).

तौबा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تَوْبَه (tawba), from Arabic تَوْبَة (tawba). Cognate with Bengali তওবা (toōba).

माफ़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مُعَاف (mu'āf), borrowed from Arabic مُعَافًى (muʕāfan), from عَافَى (ʕāfā).

अल्लाह.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اَللّٰه (allāh), from Arabic اللّٰه (allāh). First attested as Old Hindi अलह (alaha).

क़सम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian قَسَم (qasam), from Arabic قَسَم (qasam). Compare Bengali কসম (qôsom), Punjabi ਕ਼ਸਮ (qasam).

जनाब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جناب (janāb), from Arabic جَنَاب (janāb).

खेला.etym: Borrowed from Sanskrit खेला (khelā), ultimately from the root खेल् (khel).

साहब.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian صاحب (sāhib), from Arabic صَاحِب (ṣāḥib). Compare Bengali সাহেব (śaheb), Punjabi ਸਾਹਬ (sāhab) / صاحب (ṣāḥb), Gujarati સાહેબ (sāheb), Marathi साहेब (sāheb), Marwari सायब (sāyab).

मुँह.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀫𑀼𑀳 (muha), from Sanskrit मुख॑ (múkha), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *múkʰam, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *múkʰam, from *múkHam. Doublet of मुख (mukh), a tatsama.

तरह.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian طرح (tarh, “plan, design”), from Arabic طَرْح (ṭarḥ, “teaching, deduction”). Cognate with English tare (“empty weight of a container”).

ताक़तवर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian طاقتور (tāqat-var). By surface analysis, ताक़त (tāqat) + -वर (-var).

बेईमान.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بیایمان (bē-īmān, “faithless”). By surface analysis, बे- (be-) + ईमान (īmān, “faith”).

छोकरी.etym: Feminine of छोकरा (chokrā). Compare Gujarati છોકરી (chokrī).

कली.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀓𑀮𑀺𑀕 (kaliga), from Sanskrit कलिका (kalikā). Cognate with Gujarati કળી (kaḷī), Marathi कळी (kaḷī).

दीवार.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دیوار (dīwār), from Middle Persian dywʾl (dēwār). Cognate to Punjabi ਦੀਵਾਰ (dīvār).

ज़िंदा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زنده (zinda), from Middle Persian zyndk', zywndk' (zīndag, “alive”). Compare Bengali জিন্দা (jinda), Punjabi ਜਿੰਦਾ (jindā).

बेवक़ूफ़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بیوقوف (bēwuqūf), from بیـ (bē-, “without”) + Arabic وُقُوف (wuqūf, “standing still; study, knowledge”). Compare Bengali বেকুব (bekub), Gujarati બેવકૂફ (bevakūph).

लड़का.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *लडिक्क (laḍikka). Related to the lexicographically-attested Sanskrit लाडिक (lāḍika, “boy, servant”), लट्व (laṭva, “dancing boy”) लट (laṭa, “fool”), and thus may ultimately come from Sanskrit लट् (laṭ, “to act like a child”) + Middle Indo-Ar…

ख़ून.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خُون (xūn). First attested in c. 1564 as Middle Hindi خون (xvn /⁠xūn⁠/).

आँसू.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀅𑀁𑀲𑀼 (aṃsu), from Sanskrit अश्रु॑ (áśru), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Háćru, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱru, from *h₂eḱ-. Doublet of अश्रु (aśru), a tatsama.

रुलवाना.etym: Second causative form of रोना (ronā) with the suffix -वाना (-vānā).

मौत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian موت (mawt), from Arabic مَوْت (mawt). Compare Punjabi ਮੌਤ (maut).

कहीं.etym: Blend of कहाँ (kahā̃, “where”) + ही (hī, emphatic particle).

उल्लू.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀉𑀮𑀽𑀅 (ulūa) from Sanskrit उलूक (ulūka).

क्लास.etym: Borrowed from English class. Doublet of काँदना (kā̃dnā).

पसंद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پَسَنْد (pasand). Compare Assamese পছন্দ (posondo), Bengali পছন্দ (pochondo), Gujarati પસંદ (pasand), Marathi पसंत (pasanta), Punjabi ਪਸੰਦ (pasand).

नाम.etym: From Sanskrit नाम (nā́ma), borrowed from some dialect or directly from Sanskrit. The native reflex is नाँव (nā̃v). Also influenced by Classical Persian نام (nām). Cognate of English name.

अक़्ल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian عَقل ('aql), from Arabic عَقْل (ʕaql). First attested as Old Hindi अकलि (akali). Cognate with Bengali আকল (akol), Gujarati અક્કલ (akkal), Marathi अक्कल (akkal), Punjabi ਅਕ਼ਲ (aqal) / عَقل (ʻaql).

बदी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بدی (badī). By surface analysis, बद (bad) + -ई (-ī). Compare Punjabi ਬਦੀ (badī).

बदना.etym: Semi-learned borrowing from Sanskrit वद॑ति (vádati, “speaks, says, tells, adjudges, announces”).

मासूम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مَعْصُوم (ma'sūm), from Arabic مَعْصُوم (maʕṣūm, “protected”), from root ع ص م (ʕ ṣ m). Compare Turkish masum.

चिड़िया.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀘𑀺𑀟𑀺𑀕𑀸 (*ciḍigā), a feminine form from 𑀘𑀺𑀟𑀺𑀕 (ciḍiga), from Sanskrit *चिटिक (*ciṭika), चटक (caṭaka, “sparrow”). Cognate with Bengali চড়ুই (coṛui), Assamese চৰাই (sorai).

झुकना.etym: Cognate with Nepali झुक्नु (jhuknu), Punjabi ਝੁਕਣਾ (jhukṇā) / جھُکݨا (jhukṇā), Marathi झुकणे (jhukṇe).

ज़ालिम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian ظالم (zālim), from Arabic ظَالِم (ẓālim, “tyrannical, oppressing, iniquitous”). Compare Bengali জালিম (jalim).

माँ.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀫𑀸𑀤𑀸 (mādā), from Sanskrit मातृ (mātṛ, “mother”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *máHtā, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr. Doublet of माता (mātā), a tatsama. Compare Punjabi ਮਾਂ (mā̃), Gujarati મા (mā), માં (mā̃), Bengali মা (ma), Assamese মা (ma), O…

दौलत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دولت (dawlat), from Arabic دَوْلَة (dawla).

भेंट.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀪𑀺𑀝𑁆𑀝𑀸 (bhiṭṭā). See there for more. Cognate to Gujarati ભેટ (bheṭ), Marathi भेट (bheṭ), Punjabi ਭੇਂਟ (bheṇṭ) and ਭੇਟ (bheṭ).

senses.gloss: to cause one to climb, ascend

लटकाना.etym: Second causative form of लटकना (laṭaknā, “to hang, be suspended”) with the suffix -आना (-ānā).

क़ुर्बान.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian قُرْبَان (qurbān), borrowed from Arabic قُرْبَان (qurbān), borrowed from Aramaic קורבנא (qurbānā).

गाहना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit गाहदि (gāhadi), from Sanskrit गाह॑ते॒ (gā́hate).

senses.gloss: a revenue-collection area, a taraf, a tahsil

ज़बान.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زبان (zabān, zubān), from Middle Persian ŠNA / ʾwzwʾn' (uzwān), from Proto-Iranian *hižwaHs, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́iȷ́ʰwáHs. Doublet of जीभ (jībh) and जिह्वा (jihvā), possibly cognate with English tongue. Compare Odia ଜ଼ବାନ୍ (zåbān), Bengal…

जुमला.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جُمْلَه (jumla), from Arabic جُمْلَة (jumla).

तेज़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تیز (tēz), from Old Persian [script needed] (tezh). Cognate with Sanskrit तिज् (tij, “to excite, stir up, instigate”). Compare Punjabi ਤੇਜ਼ (tez).

सामने.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀁𑀫𑀼𑀳 (saṃmuha), from Sanskrit सम्मुख (sam-mukhá, “facing”). Compare with Punjabi ਸਾਹਮਣੇ (sāhmaṇe), Gujarati સામે (sāme).

सामना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀁𑀫𑀼𑀳 (saṃmuha), from Sanskrit सम्मुख (sam-mukhá, “facing”). Cognate with Marathi सामना (sāmnā), Punjabi ਸਾਹਮਣਾ (sāhmaṇā), Gujarati સામું (sāmũ) and Odia ସାମନା (sāmanā). Doublet of सम्मुख (sammukh).

गर्दन.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian گَرْدَن (gardan). First attested in c. 1635 as Middle Hindi گردن (grdn /⁠gardan⁠/). Compare Gujarati ગરદન (gardan).

ख़ामोश.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خاموش (xāmōš). Compare Bengali খামোশ (khamōś), Gujarati ખામોશ (khāmoś), Punjabi ਖ਼ਾਮੋਸ਼ (xāmoś).
Borrowed from Classical Persian خاموش (xāmōš). Compare Bengali খামোশ (khamōś), Gujarati ખામોશ (khāmoś), Punjabi ਖ਼ਾਮੋਸ਼ (xāmoś).

छुरी.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀙𑀼𑀭𑀻 (churī), from Sanskrit क्षु॒र (kṣurá), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšurás, from Proto-Indo-European *ksew- + *-rós.

senses.gloss: flow, current, stream, channel (of a river)

धार.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀥𑀸𑀭𑀸 (dhārā), from Sanskrit धारा (dhārā), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *dʰā́raH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰā́raH, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰórh₃-eh₂, from *dʰerh₃- (“to leap, spring”). Cognate with Assamese ধাৰ (dhar), Nepali धार (dhār), Gujarati ધ…

अपनाना.etym: From अपना (apnā, “oneself”) + -आना (-ānā). Cognate with Gujarati અપનાવવું (apanāvvũ, “to adopt”).

दो.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi दो (do), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑁄 (do), from Sanskrit द्व (dvá) (also duváu and duvā́), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dwáH, from Proto-Indo-European *dwóh₁. Cognate with Marathi दोन (don), Gujarati બે (be), Bengali দুই (dui), Nepali दुई (duī), Konkani दोन …

माशा.etym: Derived from Sanskrit माषक (māṣaka) or borrowed from Classical Persian ماشه (māša).

ऊपर.etym: Inherited from Apabhramsa उप्परि (uppari), from Sanskrit उ॒परि॑ (upári), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *upári, from Proto-Indo-European *upéri, from *úp + *-er. Cognate with Assamese ওপৰ (üpor).

हंस.etym: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit हं॒स (haṃsá). Doublet of हाँस (hā̃s).

लाश.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian لاش (lāš), from Middle Persian lšt (/⁠lašt⁠/, “corpse”). Compare Bengali লাশ (laś), Punjabi ਲਾਸ਼ (lāś).

दाँत.etym: Inherited from Prakrit दंत (daṃta), from Sanskrit दन्त (danta). Doublet of दंत (dant) and दंदान (dandān). Cognate with Gujarati દાંત (dā̃t), Marathi दात (dāt), Punjabi ਦੰਦ /دند (dand), Bengali দাঁত (dãt), Assamese দাঁত (dãt). Distantly cognate with English tooth, French dent.

निकालना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit णिक्कालेइ (ṇikkālei), from Sanskrit निष्कालयति (niṣkālayati). Compare Sindhi نِڪارَڻُ (nikāraṇu) / निकारणु (nikāraṇu), Nepali निकाल्नु (nikālnu), Marathi निखळणे (nikhaḷṇe).

नज़र.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian نَظَر (nazar), from Arabic نَظَر (naẓar).

senses.gloss: up to, as far as, until

लग.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi लग (laga), from Prakrit लग्ग (lagga, “connected”), from Sanskrit ल॒ग्न (lagná, “connected, intersection”). Doublet of लग्न (lagna, “wedding”) and लग्गा (laggā, “affection”). Compare also लगी (lagī, “craving”).

वास्ता.etym: Derived from Classical Persian واسطه (vâsete), from Arabic وَاسِطَة (wāsiṭa).

बिजली.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi बिजली (bijalī), बिज्जली (bijjalī), बिजुरिन (bijurina), from Prakrit विज्जुल्लिआ (vijjulliā), विज्जुल्लया (vijjullayā), from Sanskrit विद्युल्लता (vidyullatā, “forked lightning”), from विद्युत् (vidyut, “lightning”) + लता (latā, “creeper, vine, liana”),…

पीला.etym: Inherited from Prakrit पीअल (pīala, “yellow”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit पीतल (pītala), from पीत (pīta, “yellow”).

senses.gloss: to laugh [with पर (par) ‘at’], to make fun of or joke about
to be or appear cheerful or pleasant

हँसना.etym: Inherited from Apabhramsa हसइ (hasaï), from Prakrit हसइ (hasaï), from Sanskrit हसति (hásati). Cognate with Punjabi ਹੱਸਣਾ (hassaṇā), Nepali हाँस्नु (hā̃snu).

सवाल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سَوَال (sawāl, variant form of سُؤَال (su'āl)), borrowed from Arabic سُؤَال (suʔāl).

senses.gloss: an exclamation of distress; a sigh

हाय.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit हायि (hāyi). Cognate with Marathi 𑘮𑘰𑘧 (hāy) / हाय (hāy), Sindhi 𑋞𑋠𑊲 (hāi) / Sindhi हाय (hāy), Kumaoni हाइ, Punjabi ਹਾਏ (hāē) / ہائے (hā'e).

दम.etym: Last two senses, perhaps conflated with Sanskrit दम्भ (dambha).

चिल्लाना.etym: Related to किल्लाना (killānā), from Sanskrit किलकिलायति (kilakilāyati, “it cries, shrieks”), ultimately onomatopoeic. The Sanskrit root is किलकिलाय (kilakilāya).

पैर.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀬 (paya) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀭- (-ra-).

तहत.etym: Borrowed from Arabic تَحْت (taḥt, “that which is below”).

खींच.etym: From the stem of खींचना (khī̃cnā, “to pull”).Cognate with Bengali খিঁচ (khĩc)

खींचना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit *𑀔𑀺𑀁𑀘𑀇 (*khiṃcaï), 𑀔𑀁𑀘𑀇 (khaṃcaï, “to pull”), from a family of Prakrit words with "dragging" connotations of unknown further origin. Compare Punjabi ਖਿੱਚਣਾ (khiccaṇā), Gujarati ખેંચવું (kheñcvũ), Marathi खेचणे (kheċṇe), Bengali খেঁচা (khẽca).

मदद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مدد (madad), from Arabic مَدَد (madad). Compare Bengali মদত (modot), Kannada ಮದತ್ತು (madattu), Marathi मदत (madat), Nepali मदत् (madat), Odia ମଦତ୍ (madat), Punjabi ਮਦਦ (madad), Telugu మద్దతు (maddatu), Tamil மதத்து (matattu).

तमाशा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تماشا (tamāšā), ultimately from Arabic مَشَى (mašā, “to walk”). Compare Bengali তামাশা (tamaśa), Bhojpuri तमासा (tamāsā), Malayalam തമാശ (tamāśa).

काँपना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit कम्पते (kampate). Cognates include Gujarati કંપવું (kampvũ), Marwari कांपणौ (kā̃mpṇau), Assamese কঁপা (kõpa).

मजबूर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مجبور (majbūr), from Arabic مَجْبُور (majbūr).

क़त्ल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian قَتْل (qatl), from Arabic قَتْل (qatl). Compare Bengali কতল (kotol), Punjabi ਕਤਲ (katal).

आवाज़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian آوَاز (āwāz). Doublet of वाक् (vāk).

नरम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian نرم (narm). Compare Assamese নমা (noma), Bengali নরম (norom), Gujarati નરમ (naram).

वापिस.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian واپس (wāpas). Compare Punjabi ਵਾਪਸ (vāpas).

बहादुर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بهادر (bahādur). Compare Turkish bahadır. Compare Punjabi ਬਹਾਦਰ (bahādar) / بہادَر (bhādar), Gujarati બહાદુર (bahādur), Marathi बहाद्दर (bahāddar), Bengali বাহাদুর (bahadur), Turkish bahadır, Russian богаты́рь (bogatýrʹ).

वाक़ई.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian واقعی (wāqi'ī, “real; actual; true”), from Arabic واقِعِيّ (wāqiʕiyy, “actual; real”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian واقعی (wāqi'ī, “real; actual; true”), from Arabic واقِعِيّ (wāqiʕiyy, “actual; real”).

ज़बरदस्त.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian زبردست (zabardast). By surface analysis, ज़बर (zabar) + दस्त (dast).

ग़ुलाम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian غلام (ġulām), from Arabic غُلَام (ḡulām). Cognate to Bengali গোলাম (gōlam).

जूता.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀚𑀼𑀢𑁆𑀢 (jutta, “joined”), from Sanskrit युक्त (yukta, “joined, yoked”) or युक्तक (yuktaka, “pair”). Cognate with Nepali जुत्ता (juttā) and Punjabi ਜੁੱਤਾ (juttā)/جُتّا (juttā). Doublet of युक्त (yukt).

senses.gloss: to wander restlessly, to search without rest

भटकना.etym: Alternatively, somehow related to भडक्क (bhaḍakka, “sudden noise”), whence भड़कना (bhaṛaknā, “to flare up, start”).

रास्ता.etym: Compare Bengali রাস্তা (rasta), Gujarati રસ્તો (rasto), Kannada ರಸ್ತೆ (raste), Marathi रस्ता (rastā), Odia ରାସ୍ତା (rāstā), Punjabi ਰਸਤਾ (rastā).

वापस.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian واپس (wāpas). Compare Punjabi ਵਾਪਸ (vāpas).

senses.gloss: to return (to come back after some period of time, or at regular intervals)

लौटना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi लौटना (lauṭanā, “to return”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps a metathesis of Old Hindi उलटना (ulaṭanā, “to reverse”).

तय्यारा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian طیاره (tayyāra), from Ottoman Turkish طیاره (tayyare).

गिराना.etym: Causative form of गिरना (girnā) with the suffix -आना (-ānā).

महसूस.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مَحْسُوس (mahsūs), from Arabic مَحْسُوس (maḥsūs), from the root ح س س (ḥ s s). Related to एहसास (ehsās).

शोला.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian شعله (šu'la), from Arabic شُعْلَة (šuʕla).

निगलना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi निगलना (nigalanā), from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀦𑀺𑀕𑁆𑀕𑀮𑀤𑀺 (*niggaladi), from Sanskrit निगलति (nigalati, “swallows”). Cognate with Punjabi ਨਿਗਲਣਾ (niglaṇā). Doublet of लीलना (līlnā).

senses.gloss: to recite; to read out (an announcement, a poem)

पढ़ना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑀠𑀇 (paḍhaï), from Sanskrit पृथ् (pṛth). Cognate with Punjabi ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ (paṛhnā), Nepali पढ्नु (paḍhnu).

मशरिक़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مَشْرِق (mašriq), from Arabic مَشْرِق (mašriq).

senses.gloss: Mashreq (the geographic region consisting of Arabic-speaking lands in eastern Africa and western Asia, from Egypt and the Sudan eastwards).

मशरिक़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مَشْرِق (mašriq), from Arabic مَشْرِق (mašriq).

बेशर्म.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بیشرم (bē-šarm). Equivalent to बे- (be-) + शर्म (śarm, “shame”).

senses.gloss: to load, apply a burden, impose

लादना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀮𑀤𑁆𑀤𑁂𑀤𑀺 (laddedi), from Sanskrit लर्दयति (lardayati). Cognate with Punjabi ਲੱਦਣਾ (laddaṇā) / لَدّݨا (laddṇā), Sindhi لَڏَڻُ (laḏaṇu) / लॾणु, Gujarati લાદવું (lādvũ), Marathi लादणे (lādṇe).

senses.gloss: to move, to make something move

हिलाना.etym: Causative form of हिलना (hilnā). Cognate with Marathi हलवणे (halavṇe).

जान.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جان (jān), ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wyaHnás, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enh₁- (“to breathe”). Cognate with Sanskrit व्यान (vyāna). Compare Assamese জান (zan), Bengali জান (jan), Punjabi ਜਾਨ (jān).

कमज़ोर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian کمزور (kam-zōr). By surface analysis, कम- (kam-) + ज़ोर (zor).

सीना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi सीयै (sīyai), a later form of सीवै (sīvai), from Prakrit सिव्वइ (sivvaï), from Sanskrit सीव्यति (sī́vyati).

पहलवान.etym: From Classical Persian پهلوان (pahlawān). Compare Bengali পালোয়ান (palōẇan), Malayalam പയല്വാൻ (payalvāṉ), Marathi पेहलवान (pehalvān).

कोना.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit कोण (koṇa). Doublet of कोण (koṇ).

चूहा.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *चूह (cūha) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), with further origin uncertain. Perhaps an onomatopoeic word, imitating the squeaking of a mouse.

Borrowed from Classical Persian برابر (barābar). Compare Punjabi ਬਰਾਬਰ (barābar) / بَرابَر (barābar), Gujarati બરાબર (barābar), Marathi बरोबर (barobar), Bengali বরাবর (borabor).

senses.gloss: room, chamber (enclosed part of a building)

कमरा.etym: Borrowed from Portuguese câmara. Doublet of कैमरा (kaimrā, “camera”), via English.

बिठाना.etym: Transitive form of बैठना (baiṭhnā, “to sit”) with the suffix -आना (-ānā).

मुस्तक़िल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مُسْتَقِل (mustaqil), from Arabic مُسْتَقِلّ (mustaqill).

फ़ौलाद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian فولاد (fōlād, fūlād), from Middle Persian pwlʾpt' (pōlāwad).

सख़्ती.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian سَخْتِی (saxtī). By surface analysis, सख़्त (saxt) + -ई (-ī).

सिर्फ.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian صِرْف (sirf), from Arabic صِرْف (ṣirf).
Borrowed from Classical Persian صِرْف (sirf), from Arabic صِرْف (ṣirf).

बल्कि.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بلکه (balki), from Arabic بَلْ (bal) + Classical Persian که (ki).

हज़ार.etym: Compare Assamese হাজাৰ (hazar), Bengali হাজার (hajar), Gujarati હજાર (hajār), Marathi हजार (hajār), Punjabi ਹਜ਼ਾਰ (hazār), Santali ᱦᱟᱡᱟᱨ (hajar).

पनाह.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پناه (panāh), from Middle Persian 𐭯𐭭𐭠𐭧 (panāh). Compare Bengali পানা (pana), Punjabi ਪਨਾਹ (panāh).

अहाता.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian اِحَاطَه (ihāta), borrowed from Arabic إِحَاطَة (ʔiḥāṭa), from أَحَاطَ (ʔaḥāṭa).

छः.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi षट (ṣaṭa), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀙 (cha), from Ashokan Prakrit *𑀙 (*cha), 𑀱 (ṣa), from Sanskrit षष् (ṣáṣ), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *ṣwáṭṣ, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *šwáćš, from Proto-Indo-European *swéḱs. Cognate with Marathi सहा (sahā), Gujarati છ (cha)…

बजना.etym: From earlier बाजना (bājnā), from Prakrit वज्जइ (vajjaï), from Sanskrit वाद्यते (vādyate), the passive form of वादयति (vādayati), from the root वद् (vad, “to speak”). Compare Nepali बज्नु (bajnu), Gujarati વાગવું (vāgvũ), Marathi वाजणे (vāj̈ṇe), Assamese বাজা (baza), Sinhalese …

पाँच.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi पंच (paṃca), पांच (pāṃca), from Sanskrit पञ्च॑ (páñca). Cognate with Punjabi ਪੰਜ (pañj), Marathi पाच (pāc), Konkani पांच (pāñca), Nepali पाँच (pā̃c), Bengali পাঁচ (pãc), Gujarati પાંચ (pā̃c), and distantly English five. Related to पंजा (pañjā, “paw, gr…

भारी.etym: Directly borrowed from Sanskrit भारी (bhārī) or inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀪𑀸𑀭𑀺𑀕 (*bhāriga), from Sanskrit भारिक (bhārika, “heavy”). By surface analysis, भार (bhār) + -ई (-ī).

भारा.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀪𑀸𑀭 (bhāra), from Sanskrit भार (bhārá).

मर्दाना.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مردانه (mardāna), equivalent to मर्द (mard) + -आना (-ānā).

झपट.etym: Related with झपटना (jhapaṭnā, “to swoop down; to go quickly”) and झपाट (jhapāṭ, “quickness”).

senses.gloss: to swoop, pounce, plunge, raid, rush

झपटना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *झप्प- (jhappa-) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀝𑁆𑀝- (-ṭṭa-). Cognate with Marathi झपाटणे (jhapāṭṇe). Related to झपकना (jhapaknā, “to spring up”).

मेज़.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian میز (mēz, mīz), with possible influence from Portuguese mesa. Compare Marathi मेज (mej̈).

समझ.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀁𑀩𑀼𑀚𑁆𑀛 (saṃbujjha). By surface analysis, deverbal form of समझना (samajhnā). Cognate with Marathi समज (samaj).

खोलना.etym: From Proto-New Indo-Aryan *खोल्लइ (khŏllaï) of uncertain origin. See there for more. Cognate with Bengali খোলা (khōla), Gujarati ખોલવું (kholvũ), and Nepali खोल्नु (kholnu).

senses.gloss: pallu, the decorative, loose end of a sari or dupatta that hangs over the shoulder

गिरना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi गिरना (giranā), from Prakrit *𑀕𑀺𑀭𑀇 (*giraï), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷelH- (“drip”). Related to गलना (galnā, “to melt, ooze”) and डिगना (ḍignā, “to falter”).

senses.gloss: be (name of the second letter of the Perso-Arabic alphabet).

ख़ुदकुशी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خودکشی (xwadkušī). By surface analysis, ख़ुद (xud, “self”) + कुशी (kuśī, “killing”).

तैयार.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تیار (tayyār), from Arabic طَيَّار (ṭayyār). Compare Gujarati તૈયાર (taiyār), Marathi तयार (tayār), Punjabi ਤਿਆਰ (tiāra), Malayalam തയ്യാർ (tayyāṟ), Tamil தயார் (tayār).

हालत.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian حالت (hālat), from Arabic حَالَة (ḥāla).

senses.gloss: the cross, on which Jesus Christ was crucified

सूली.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀲𑀽𑀮𑀺𑀆 (sūliā), from Sanskrit शूलिका (śūlikā).

घड़ियाल.etym: Inherited from Sanskrit घण्टिक (ghaṇṭika) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀮𑁆𑀮- (-lla-).

भयानक.etym: From Sanskrit भयानक (bhayānaka), ultimately related to भय (bhay).

गुनगुनाना.etym: Onomatopoeic reduplication. Compare Nepali गुनगुनाउनु (gunagunāunu), Marathi गुणगुणणे (guṇguṇṇe).

senses.gloss: the ways or acts of God in the mortal realm

लीलना.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀦𑀺𑀕𑀺𑀮𑀤𑀺 (*nigiladi), from Sanskrit *निगिलति (*nigilati), a variant of निगलति (nigalati, “swallows”). Cognate with Pali niggilati and Nepali निल्नु (nilnu). Doublet of निगलना (nigalnā). On the assimilation of initial n > l in Hindi based on the…

senses.gloss: Shri Rāma, the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu
a male given name, Ram and Rāma, from Sanskrit
a whistle (sound), the act of whistling

सीटी.etym: Related to Sanskrit शीत् (śīt). Cognate with Marathi शिट्टी (śiṭṭī).

senses.gloss: quite, at all, wholly, absolutely, utterly

बिल्कुल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بِالْکُلّ (bi-l-kull), Arabic بِالْكُلّ (bi-l-kull).

बच्चा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بَچَّه (bačča), from Proto-Iranian *wacáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *watsás, from Proto-Indo-European *wetsós, from *wétos + *-ós. Doublet of बछड़ा (bachṛā, “calf, child, boy”).

गहरा.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀕𑀳𑀻𑀭 (gahīra), from Sanskrit गभीर (gabhīrá), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gabʰrás, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂bʰ-.

बारीक.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian باریک (bārīk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (bʾlyk /⁠bārīk/, /bārīg⁠/). Compare Punjabi ਬਰੀਕ (barīk) / بَرِیک (barīk), Gujarati બારીક (bārīk), Marathi बारीक (bārīk), Sylheti ꠛꠣꠞꠤꠇ (barik).

मोटा.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *मोट्ट (mŏṭṭa), perhaps from a lost substrate. Cognate with Bengali মোটা (mōṭa), Punjabi ਮੋਟਾ (moṭā).

senses.gloss: grip, hold, grasp (such as in wrestling)

पकड़ना.etym: Inherited from Old Hindi पकडि (pakaḍi), पाकडि (pākaḍi), from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *पक्कडइ (pakkaḍaï), perhaps further from Prakrit पग्ग- (pagga-, “seizes”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-). Cognate to Gujarati પકડવું (pakaḍvũ), Marathi पकडणे (pakaḍṇe).

senses.gloss: track, trace (of something dragged along); skid
to implicate, involve, draw into a scheme

घसीटना.etym: McGregor suggests a relation to Sanskrit घर्षति (gharṣati, “to rub”).

ख़ुशामद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian خشآمد (xʷuš-āmad). Equivalent to ख़ुश (xuś) + आमद (āmad).

मांगना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀫𑀕𑁆𑀕𑀇 (maggaï), from Sanskrit मार्ग॑ति (mā́rgati), from मार्ग (mārga), a vṛddhi derivative of मृग (mṛga), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *mr̥gás. Cognate with Marathi मागणे (māgṇe).

फड़फड़ाना.etym: Ultimately from a Proto-Indo-Aryan *phaṭ (“sudden noise”); a reduplication. Compare Marathi फडफडणे (phaḍphaḍṇe, “to flutter”).

नसना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit णस्सइ (ṇassaï), from Sanskrit नश्य॑ति (náśyati). Related to नाठ (nāṭh), नाठना (nāṭhnā).

नस.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀡𑀲𑀸 (ṇasā), from Sanskrit स्नसा (snasā, “tendon, muscle”).

senses.gloss: conceit, arrogance, vanity (excessive self-esteem; disregard for the opinions of others)

अकड़.etym: Cognate with Marathi अकड (akaḍ), Punjabi ਆਕੜ / آکَڑ (ākaṛ), Pahari-Potwari آکَڑ (ākaṛ).

आन.etym: Inherited from Prakrit अण्ण (aṇṇa, “other”), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀅𑀁𑀜 (aṃña), from Sanskrit अन्य॑ (ánya).
Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit [Term?], from Sanskrit आणि (āṇi, “axle-pin; boundary”).

दरवाज़ा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دَرْوَازَه (darwāza). Compare Assamese দৰ্জা (dorza), Bengali দরজা (dorja), Gujarati દરવાજો (darvājo), Kashmiri दरवाज़ॖ (darawāzụ), Marathi दरवाजा (darvājā), Punjabi ਦਰਵਾਜ਼ਾ (darvāzā).

senses.gloss: purdah (traditional Indian system of segragating women from men through the use of purdahs (veils))

पर्दा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian پَرْدَه (parda). Doublet of पट (paṭ) and पटका (paṭkā). Compare Bengali পর্দা (porda), Malayalam പർദ്ദ (paṟdda).

देर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دیر (dēr), from Old Persian 𐎭𐎼𐎥 (darga), from Proto-Iranian *dr̥Hgáh (compare Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬔𐬀 (dar^əga, “long”)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dr̥Hgʰás (compare Sanskrit दीर्घ (dīrghá)), from Proto-Indo-European *dl̥h₁gʰós (compare Latin longus, Old …

ताक़त.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian طَاقَت (tāqat, “stamina, endurance”), from Arabic طَاقَة (ṭāqa). Compare Gujarati તાકત (tākat), Kannada ತಾಕತ್ತು (tākattu), Marathi ताकद (tākad), Punjabi ਤਾਕਤ (tākat) / طَاقَت (t̤āqat).

अलमारी.etym: Borrowed from Portuguese almario or armário, from Latin armarium (“closet, chest”), from arma (“weapons, tools”) + -ārium (“denoting a place where things are kept”).

हटना.etym: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *हट्टइ (haṭṭaï) of uncertain origin. See there for more.

बाज़ू.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بازو (bāzū, “arm”), from Old Persian 𐎲𐎠𐏀𐎢 (bāzu), from Proto-Iranian *baHjúh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰaHȷ́ʰúš, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂ǵʰus (“arm”). Doublet of बाँह (bā̃h) and बाहु (bāhu). Cognate with Kannada ಬಾಜು (bāju).

senses.gloss: the human being smuggled in human smuggling

कबूतर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian کَبُوتَر (kabūtar). Doublet of कपोत (kapot).

दाना.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian دانه (dāna). Compare Bengali দানা (dana), Nepali दाना (dānā), Punjabi ਦਾਣਾ (dāṇā).

टँगना.etym: Intransitive form of टाँगना (ṭāṅgnā), from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *टंगइ (ṭaṃgaï). Compare Punjabi ਟਾਂਗਣਾ (ṭāṅgṇā).

तस्वीर.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تَصْوِیر (taswīr), borrowed from Arabic تَصْوِير (taṣwīr), from صَوَّرَ (ṣawwara). Compare Gujarati તસવીર (tasvīr), Punjabi ਤਸਵੀਰ (tasvīr).

senses.gloss: an outer covering; case, sheath, cover, shell

बंद.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بَنْد (band). Doublet of बंध (bandh).
Borrowed from Classical Persian بَنْد (band). Doublet of बंध (bandh).

चेहरा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian چِهْرَه (čihra), from Middle Persian 𐭰𐭧𐭫𐭪𐭩 (čihrag). Doublet of चित्र (citra) and चीता (cītā). Compare Assamese চেহেৰা (sehera), Bengali চেহারা (cehara), Gujarati ચહેરો (cahero), Marathi चेहरा (cehrā), Punjabi ਚਿਹਰਾ (cihrā).

senses.gloss: to wobble, stagger, sway; to stumble

क़दम.etym: Borrowed from Arabic قَدَم (qadam). Compare Bengali কদম (kodom).

लम्बा.etym: Inherited from Prakrit लंब (laṃba) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-) without cluster simplification—for which compare लाँबा (lāmbā) and लाँब (lāmb)—, from Sanskrit लम्ब (lamba). Cognate with Marathi लांब (lāmba).

नया.etym: Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀡𑀯𑀺𑀅 (ṇavia) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from Sanskrit नविय (náviya), नव्य (návya) (whence Bhojpuri नया (nayā)), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *náwyas, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *náwyas (whence Kamkata-viri nuĩ), from Proto-Indo-European *néwyos (whe…

उंगली.etym: Regular metathesis of अंगुली (aṅgulī), from Prakrit 𑀅𑀁𑀕𑀼𑀮𑀺 (aṃguli), from Sanskrit अ॒ङ्गुलि॑ (aṅgúli). For other examples of such metathesis, compare इमली (imlī), खुजली (khujlī). Cognate with Assamese আঙুলি (aṅuli), Bengali আঙুল (aṅul), Dhivehi އިނގިލި (iⁿgili), Gujarati આંગળી…

कान.etym: Inherited from Apabhramsa 𑖎𑖜𑖿𑖜 (kaṇṇa), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀓𑀡𑁆𑀡 (kaṇṇa), from Sanskrit कर्ण (karṇa, “ear”). Doublet of कर्ण (karṇ).

senses.gloss: Cannes (a city in Alpes-Maritimes department, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, southeastern France).

जिस्म.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian جِسْم (jism), from Arabic جِسْم (jism). Cognate with Bengali জেসম (jesm)

नग़मा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian نغمه (naġma), itself from Arabic نَغْمة (naḡma).

senses.gloss: a female given name, Naghma, from Arabic

नग़मा.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian نغمه (naġma), itself from Arabic نَغْمة (naḡma).

पुतली.etym: Inherited from Middle Hindi پتلی (ptly /⁠putlī⁠/) (c. 1625), from Old Hindi पुतरी (putarī), from Apabhramsa पुत्तलिय (puttaliya), from Prakrit पुत्तलिआ (puttaliā), from पुत्त (putta) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀮- (-la-) + -𑀇𑀓𑀸- (-ikā-).. By surface analysis, पुतला (putlā) + -ई (-ī).

मुर्ग़ी.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian مرغ (murġ), from Middle Iranian *murɣ (“bird”).

मालूम.etym: Borrowed from Arabic مَعْلُوم (maʕlūm), from عَلِمَ (ʕalima).

बुज़दिल.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian بزدل (buz-dil), from بز (buz, “goat”) + دل (dil, “heart”).
Borrowed from Classical Persian بزدل (buz-dil), from بز (buz, “goat”) + دل (dil, “heart”).

उतरना.etym: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀉𑀢𑁆𑀢𑀭𑀇 (uttaraï), from Sanskrit उत्त॑रति (úttarati), from उद्- (ud-) + तर॑ति (tárati).

दिखाना.etym: Causative form of दिखना (dikhnā, “to be seen”)

तालीम.etym: Borrowed from Classical Persian تَعْلِیم (ta'līm), borrowed from Arabic تَعْلِيم (taʕlīm), from عَلَّمَ (ʕallama).

होंठ.etym: Inherited from Prakrit होट्ठ (hŏṭṭha). See there for more. Compare ओठ (oṭh, “lip”).
